verdicts.explanation: The abstract states a total room-temperature conductivity of 2.03 mS cm−1 for the 1 wt% MgF2 NASICON with an activation energy of 0.277 eV, and the 1250 °C sintering temperature is given in Section 2.1.

The introduction gives the bare NASICON's ionic conductivity as 1.12 mS/cm, measured by the authors in this work, with no temperature stated (so null is correct). The z=0 activation energy of 0.311 eV is stated in Section 3.
Section 3 states that the bulk conductivity of the bare sample is 2.58 mS/cm at 25 °C, and the unit appears in the following text as the record notes.
Section 3 states that the grain-boundary conductivity of the bare sample is 1.99 mS/cm at 25 °C.
Section 3 states that at z = 1 the bulk conductivity reaches 3.3 mS/cm, measured at 25 °C in Fig. 2b, and the unit is mS/cm.

The paper does report a grain-boundary conductivity of 5.28 mS/cm for z = 1 at 25 °C, so the record matches the text. The value is larger than the total conductivity of 2.03 mS/cm, which is internally odd, but the record faithfully reflects what is stated.
The paper states the biggest bulk conductivity is 3.74 mS/cm for the z = 0.75 sample, and the Fig. 2b discussion gives the measurement at 25 °C.
The paper states the lowest bulk conductivity is 2.46 mS/cm when z = 3, and the Fig. 2b discussion gives the measurement at 25 °C.
